title: Wartime foundry work and plans to buy a dump truck
summary: Turned down for the army over his knees, Monk saved to start a trucking business, encouraged by a neighbor with a dump truck.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, it came later for me, so far as the music. I continued doing what I was doing. What I was doing, I was doing it very well but it didn't have the same meaning...it wasn't what life was about. I had strong thoughts at that time, really really strong thoughts of...Prior to that, to show you how things work, I was very successful at doing what I was doing in terms of a lay person and money. But at that time it was, like, after the war (started), 1941 There was a lot of work.

I wasn't inducted into the army or anything. I was turned down because I had knee problems, no reflex in the knees or something. Anyhow, I remember, I was working, making good money, working Saturdays and Sundays and overtime. Just, if you can call it, making good.

And I saved my money. I bought a piece of property and we started, we built our home. And I started another savings because I was going to go into a business for myself. I had a goal I wanted to achieve. And at the time I thought... I had sort of like chosen that it...something that I think I really wanted to be into...I was gonna buy a dump truck. Go into trucking, that kind of business, construction.

Because there was a guy living across the street from me, and he was a black man and he had a dump truck. And he was sand and gravel-type thing, because of road construction and building going on, quite a bit of it. And he was one of the very few blacks that were able to get contracts here or there, to work independently. And I had some conversation with him. He said, 'Well...' and he was a nice man, and he would say, 'Montgomery, you're a nice fella and you could do so-and-so-and-so, and I'll be happy to introduce you to certain people so maybe you could make it in that.' I could...he was trying to encourage me of getting this dump truck because if you were lucky...it was during that time, too, if a black man could have a decent chance of being an independent business man. And I could have built the business. I could have one truck and bought another truck and bought another truck. So here I'm trying to see myself with a string of trucks, in the trucking business.
Well, that's balanced against something that really wasn't very...
